questions.question: How many services does AWS offer according to the lecture?
questions.reference_answer: AWS offers over 200 fully featured services from data centers globally.

questions.question: What are the five EC2 instance types, with an example of each?
questions.reference_answer: General Purpose (t3, m5), Compute Optimized (c5), Memory Optimized (r5), Storage Optimized (i3) and Accelerated Computing (p4).

questions.question: What are the steps for launching an EC2 instance?
questions.reference_answer: Select an AMI, choose an instance type, configure instance details, add storage, configure security settings.

questions.question: What is an Amazon Machine Image (AMI)?
questions.reference_answer: A pre-configured template for EC2 instances that includes the OS, applications and configurations; users can create custom AMIs.

questions.question: What are the three components of Auto Scaling?
questions.reference_answer: The Auto Scaling Group (a logical grouping of EC2 instances), the Launch Configuration/Template (defines the instance configuration) and Scaling Policies (rules for scaling in and out).
key_points: Auto Scaling Group: logical grouping of EC2 instances
Scaling Policies: rules for scaling in and out

questions.question: What are the key features of Amazon CloudWatch?
questions.reference_answer: Metrics (real-time monitoring), Logs (centralized logging), Alarms (automated alerts and actions), Dashboards (customizable visualizations) and Events (detect and react to changes).
key_points: Events: detect and react to changes

questions.question: Which AWS storage option should I pick if several servers need to read and write the same files at once?
questions.reference_answer: Amazon EFS: a scalable, fully managed NFS file system with shared access for multiple EC2 instances.
key_points: shared access for multiple EC2 instances

questions.question: Where should I keep old records that I must store for years but almost never need to open?
questions.reference_answer: Amazon S3 Glacier: low-cost archival storage for long-term backup and archiving, with retrieval times from minutes to hours.

questions.question: How can AWS add servers ahead of time before a busy period it expects?
questions.reference_answer: Predictive scaling forecasts future traffic and scales in advance; scheduled scaling scales based on a schedule.
key_points: predictive scaling forecasts future traffic and scales in advance

questions.question: How do I spread visitors across several EC2 servers so one server failing does not take the site down?
questions.reference_answer: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances, improving fault tolerance and availability; it is best combined with Auto Scaling and health checks.
key_points: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across multiple EC2 instances

questions.question: How can I get an email when my server's CPU goes above a limit?
questions.reference_answer: Create a CloudWatch alarm with a threshold on a metric such as CPUUtilization; alarms trigger notifications through Amazon SNS or actions such as Auto Scaling.
key_points: CloudWatch alarm sets a threshold on a metric
alarms trigger notifications via Amazon SNS

questions.question: In the CloudWatch Dashboards slide, what do the boxes in the flowchart say, in order?
questions.reference_answer: Create customized views of metrics, then visualize application and infrastructure health, then share dashboards across teams.

questions.question: What are the benefits of EC2, and which pricing models does it offer?
questions.reference_answer: Benefits: scalability and flexibility, cost-effective pricing models, secure and reliable, various instance types. Pricing models: On-Demand, Reserved, Spot Instances, Savings Plans, Dedicated Hosts.
key_points: On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, Savings Plans, Dedicated Hosts

questions.question: Which AWS database services are mentioned, and which compute services?
questions.reference_answer: Database: Amazon RDS and DynamoDB. Compute: Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda.

questions.question: What are the best practices for Auto Scaling, and what are its typical use cases?
questions.reference_answer: Best practices: use health checks to replace unhealthy instances, combine with ELB, use CloudWatch for monitoring, test scaling policies regularly. Use cases: web applications with variable traffic, batch processing, e-commerce sites during sales/events.
key_points: variable-traffic web apps, batch processing, e-commerce during sales
